title: Starfall, a browser game built from scratch
name: Starfall
what: a small browser game called Starfall
details: In the game you steer a little ship along the bottom of the screen, dodge falling stars and catch energy orbs, and the stars fall faster as the score climbs.
plan: a finished game with a start screen, score, levels, keyboard and touch controls, and sound that stays off until the player turns it on

title: Orrery, the solar system in motion
name: Orrery
what: an orrery called Orrery: the Sun and its eight planets moving on a canvas
details: Each planet goes round in its true order and at its true relative speed (the distances may be squeezed so that every orbit fits on the screen). A slider sets how fast time runs, the date the model is showing is printed in a corner, and clicking a planet opens a small card with a few facts about it, written into the code.
plan: a finished orrery with labelled orbits, the time slider, the date, pause and play, and a facts card for every planet

title: Life Lab, Conway's Game of Life to play with
name: Life Lab
what: a Game of Life laboratory called Life Lab
details: A grid of cells follows Conway's rules. The player draws and erases cells with the mouse or a finger, starts, pauses and steps the world one generation at a time, sets the speed, and drops in classic patterns from a small gallery: a glider, a pulsar, a lightweight spaceship and the Gosper glider gun. Counters show the generation and how many cells are alive.
plan: a finished lab with drawing, play and pause, single steps, speed, the pattern gallery and the counters

title: Labyrinth, a maze that builds and solves itself
name: Labyrinth
details: The page carves a new maze one step at a time so the viewer watches it grow, then finds the way from the top-left corner to the bottom-right and draws the path. There are buttons for a new maze and for the maze's size, a choice between two ways of solving it (breadth-first search and A*), and a count of how many cells each way looked at before it found the exit.
plan: a finished page that carves, animates and solves mazes both ways and shows their counts

title: Sortbars, sorting you can watch
name: Sortbars
details: Bars of different heights are sorted on screen one comparison at a time, with the two bars being compared lit up, by bubble sort, insertion sort, merge sort and quicksort. The player picks the algorithm, the number of bars and the speed, and the page counts comparisons and swaps, so the algorithms can be compared side by side.
plan: a finished visualiser with all four algorithms, the controls and the counts

title: Blockfall, a falling-blocks puzzle
name: Blockfall
what: a falling-blocks puzzle game called Blockfall
details: Shapes made of four squares fall into a well ten squares wide and twenty tall. The player moves and turns them with the keyboard or with touch buttons, full rows clear and score, the fall speeds up every ten rows, the next shape is shown beside the well, and the best score is kept in the browser's local storage.
plan: a finished game with a start screen, pause, scoring, levels, the next-shape preview, touch buttons and a game-over screen with the best score

title: Pixelsmith, a pixel-art editor
name: Pixelsmith
details: A canvas of 32 by 32 big pixels, a palette of sixteen colours, a pencil, an eraser, a flood fill and a colour picker, undo and redo, a grid that can be turned off, and a live preview at actual size. The drawing is kept in the browser's local storage so it survives a reload, and the page opens with a small example drawing so the screen is never empty.
plan: a finished editor with every tool, undo and redo, the preview and the saved drawing

title: Beatgrid, a drum machine in the browser
name: Beatgrid
details: A grid of sixteen steps for six sounds (kick, snare, closed hat, open hat, clap and a tone), every sound made in code with the Web Audio API, with no sample files. Clicking a cell turns it on or off, a playhead sweeps across at the tempo, the tempo can be changed, and there are a few preset beats. Sound stays off until the player presses Start, and the grid lights up as it plays, so it reads on a silent screen too.
plan: a finished sequencer with all six sounds, the playhead, tempo, presets and the Start button
